items.justification: Resilience to power and network outages versus accessible guidance on system configuration.
Both keep users informed so they can maintain a secure state; A through checking guidance, B through proactive update notices.
Both protect sensitive data from unauthorized access, A on the wire, B wherever training and test data are held.
Authentication before network access versus secure deletion at decommissioning.
Using reviewed implementations versus passing test findings to downstream operators.
Both require advance notice to users before an update lands, A when it disrupts function, B whenever a model is updated.
Recognizable model designation versus secure coding training for developers.
Cryptographic strength of authentication versus secure deletion at decommissioning.
Prohibiting hard-coded security parameters versus an audit log of configuration changes.
Both require accessible disclosure of what the product does with data, A of sensing capabilities, B of where and how data is used and stored.
Vulnerability disclosure policy versus evaluation of access control frameworks.
Hardware memory access control versus asset tracking and version control.
Best practice cryptography for communication versus justifying use of poorly documented components.
Both establish authenticity of a distributed artefact; A obliges the recipient to verify, B obliges the publisher to release the hashes.
Password generation mechanism versus transparency about data use and storage.
Both publish maintenance commitments, A the support period to users, B the design and post-deployment plans to downstream parties.
User control over update notifications versus protection of sensitive training data.
Detection of and response to software tampering versus general robustness to adversarial input and system failure.
Informing users of a needed update and planning for the case where no update exists are the two branches of managing unpatched risk.
Orderly network reconnection versus separation of development and tuning environments.
Authentication before configuration change versus the required content of model documentation.
Disabling debug interfaces versus general robustness of the model to adversarial input.
Both prevent internals leaking through an exposed channel, A through network interface disclosure, B through model outputs.
Setup guidance for consumers versus contingency planning where updates cannot be provided.
Authentication on a configuration interface versus confidentiality of training and test data; different assets.
Secure boot verification versus incident management and recovery planning.
Both are accessible disclosures to users but of unrelated content: support duration versus data handling.
Instructions for deleting personal data versus security testing before release.
Documenting sensing capabilities for users versus an internal audit trail shared with downstream operators.
Both govern the engineering discipline applied to released software; A the development process, B re-testing after a major change.
User control over automatic updates versus due diligence on external components.
Secure storage of security parameters versus logging of system and user actions.
Timely remediation of vulnerabilities versus sharing documentation with End-users.
Choice of machine-to-machine authentication method versus an organizational access control review.
Both require the user to be told, in an accessible and recognizable way, that a security update applies and what it addresses; the scope is the same.
Password generation mechanism versus documentation of public training data provenance.
Boot-time verification and the process that authenticates and version-controls assets serve one component integrity control from opposite ends.
Vulnerability disclosure policy versus the security content of model documentation.
Declaring the support period and actually supplying patches within it are separate obligations that together constitute update support.
Tamper resistance of a device identity versus monitoring model behaviour over time.
